## Example 2.2 {#dc2-example-2-2 .dc-lesson .dc-proof}

<p>Consider the function <span data-math="y=\log_a x"></span> where <span data-math="a"></span> is a constant, <span data-math="a>0"></span>, <span data-math="a\ne1"></span>, and <span data-math="x>0"></span>.</p>
<div class="dc-proof-layout"><div class="dc-proof-prompts">
<p><strong>a)</strong> Use the change-of-base formula to rewrite <span data-math="\log_a x"></span> in terms of natural logarithms (<span data-math="\ln"></span>):</p>
<p><strong>b)</strong> Differentiate the resulting expression with respect to <span data-math="x"></span>, treating <span data-math="\frac1{\ln a}"></span> as a constant multiplier:</p>
<p><strong>c)</strong> Hence, deduce the final formula:</p>
</div><div class="dc-proof-working fragment" data-fragment-index="0">
<p><span data-math="\log_a x=\frac{\ln x}{\ln a}"></span></p>
<p><span data-math="\frac{d}{dx}(\log_a x)=\frac{d}{dx}\left(\frac1{\ln a}\cdot\ln x\right)"></span></p>
<p><span data-math="=\frac1{\ln a}\cdot\frac1x"></span></p>
<p class="dc-final-rule"><span data-math="\frac{d}{dx}(\log_a x)=\frac1{x\ln a}"></span></p>
</div></div><p class="booklet-cue">Booklet p. 9 · Example 2.2</p>

::: notes
(a) Change base to ln x/ln a. (b) The factor 1/ln a is constant because a is constant; its derivative is not needed. (c) The derivative is 1/(x ln a). Domains: x>0, a>0, a≠1. For a=e, ln e=1 recovers 1/x. Compare Lesson 1: exponential derivatives multiply by ln a; logarithmic derivatives divide by ln a. The conversion and all differentiation working reveal together on Next, after students attempt them in OneNote. Previous hides the whole group. About four minutes.
:::
